betterCitation: William Wordsworth, Lines written a few miles above Tintern Abbey, lines 34 to 36, Lyrical Ballads (J. and A. Arch, 1798)
reason: Wording holds: Project Gutenberg 9622 and the Wikisource 1798 page both print the three lines exactly as quoted, semicolon after life, no comma after unremembered, and these are the 1798 readings (the later text has a comma after life and after unremembered). The locator does not hold. The verifier counts the passage at 35 to 37 by treating the half line Though absent long, (printed on its own indented line as a new verse paragraph) as a line of its own, while at the same time giving the standard text as 33 to 35, which is only true when the equivalent half line These beauteous forms, is joined to The Hermit sits alone. as one line 22. The two counts use different conventions. The 1798 text has exactly one more line than the later text before this passage (four lines at Which, at this season ... The wild green landscape against three in the revision), so by the convention that gives the standard text 33 to 35 the 1798 passage is 34 to 36, which is also what the proposal had for the 1798 count (its error was in the standard number). I counted it twice from the transcription: 36 physical lines to His little, nameless, unremembered acts counting the half line separately, 35 counting it joined. shipped.js: not shipped, no near line, Wordsworth at 0 for the year, not banned.
